beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book begins with an assignment, before explaining the machinery underneath it.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: You first meet the worker and the shared workplace.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: You then explore applications in software, research, browser work, and documents.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The middle chapters ask how delegated work becomes repeatable and controllable.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Only then does the book unpack deployment, tools, and execution environments.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its final chapter examines the wider platform, its risks, and its research directions.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: This order lets practical questions give meaning to technical choices.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: You can read the architecture as a response to work, rather than memorize components.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: One distinction gives a clear taste of the book’s approach.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A Robot is the persistent virtual worker, with a role and history.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: An AI Agent is the reasoning-and-action software it uses.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A Ploinky Agent is a deployable package containing capabilities such as agents or tools.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: These terms describe different responsibilities, even when ordinary conversation mixes them together.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The surprising consequence is that replacing the intelligence need not erase the worker.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The project, permissions, and accepted work should retain their continuity.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Reading this distinction closely gives you a way to question dependence on particular software.
